samples.text:
The line graph shows the change of average house prices in three city, City X, City Y and City Z, from 2000 to 2020. The prices is shown as an index and 2000 is 100.

City X had the biggest increase. Its index went up to 150 in 2004 and 185 in 2008. Then it dropped to 160 in 2012 but after that it rose again and reached 255 in 2020, that is the highest on the graph.

City Y also increased but not so much. It rose to 140 in 2008 and then fell to 115 in 2012. After 2012 it increased again slowly and it was 150 in 2020.

City Z was different from the other cities. It increased a little to 105 in 2004, but then it decreased to 98 in 2008 and 80 in 2012. In 2016 it was 92 and in 2020 it finally rose to 118.

Overall, the house prices in all three cities went up during the period but City X went up the most, and all cities fell between 2008 and 2012.
samples.why: Basic overview placed at the end · key features and the shared fall covered · simple, repetitive vocabulary · errors in plurals, agreement and relative clauses that do not block communication.

samples.text:
The graph shows how average house prices changed in three cities between 2000 and 2020, with the figures expressed as an index where 2000 equals 100.

Overall, house prices were higher in all three cities by the end of the period, although City X experienced much stronger growth than the other two. Another clear feature is that prices in every city fell between 2008 and 2012 before recovering.

City X saw a rapid increase at first, with its index rising to 150 in 2004 and 185 in 2008. After falling back to 160 in 2012, prices resumed their upward trend and reached 255 by 2020, which means they were more than two and a half times their 2000 level.

City Y followed a similar pattern but at a much lower level. Its index went up to 140 in 2008, dropped to 115 in 2012 and then increased steadily to 150. City Z, however, performed the weakest. After a small rise to 105 in 2004, prices fell below the base level, hitting a low of 80 in 2012. They then recovered gradually, finishing at 118 in 2020, only 18% more than in 2000.
samples.why: Clear overview of overall growth and the shared downturn · key features highlighted · logical paragraphing · accurate derived comparisons · good vocabulary and generally accurate grammar with a minor superlative slip.

samples.text:
The line graph traces movements in average house prices in Cities X, Y and Z over the two decades from 2000, using an index in which the 2000 price level is set at 100.

Overall, prices ended the period higher in all three cities, but the extent of growth varied greatly, with City X far outperforming the others. It is also evident that all three markets suffered a downturn between 2008 and 2012.

City X experienced the most dramatic appreciation. Its index surged to 185 by 2008, and although it slipped to 160 in 2012, the recovery that followed was vigorous, pushing the index to 255 in 2020. In other words, house prices there rose by 155% over the twenty years.

City Y displayed the same general shape on a smaller scale, climbing to 140 in 2008, falling to 115 in 2012 and then recovering to 150. City Z, by contrast, stagnated for much of the period. After edging up to 105 in 2004, its prices dropped below their original level, bottoming out at 80 in 2012, and they did not exceed the base figure again until the final year, when the index stood at 118.
samples.why: Skilful selection of key features and contrasts · clear, well-placed overview · accurate figures and correct percentage derivation · wide, precise vocabulary ('appreciation', 'stagnated') · varied, error-free structures.
